move: split-flap cells cycle characters row by row, clock ticks, top row departs
how: A dark board with a header and clock, column labels and five rows of flap cells (time, destination, flight, gate) plus a status pill. The board rises in (expo.out), the header text and rows fade in. From 8% each flap runs a proxy tween of 6 to 13 steps at 0.07s per step whose onUpdate writes the next character from a seeded alphabet, landing on its target, while a paired scaleY 0.6 to 1 pulse repeats per step; rows start 0.28s apart and columns cascade 0.03s per flap. Status labels rise through masks 0.28s apart. A proxy tween drives the clock seconds for the whole clip; at 58% one status slides up, swaps to BOARDING with a colour change and slides back. At 81% the top row slides out x -60 fading (power3.in), the others shuffle up y -72 (expo.inOut) and the board fades.
adapt: Change DATA rows (widths per column are fixed in cell()), the alphabet, colours and brand footer; keep the 0.07s step cadence and the 0.28s row cascade.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the rows and flap cells and returns the flap list; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline; the character cycling already runs from onUpdate proxy tweens so it ports directly. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: around 130 flaps each with two tweens; heavy timeline
not a true 3D flap flip: the .n/.t/.b markup is unused and the flip is a scaleY pulse
